name: Exhicon Events Media Solutions Limited
sector: Exhibition and event infrastructure; venue development; UAE contracting and aviation
identity_note: ISIN and BSE543895 confirmed by signed issuer filings; main-board migration completion not verified.
summary: Exhicon supplies event and exhibition infrastructure and is expanding into owned or operated venues, UAE contracting and aviation. FY2026 reported revenue of ₹202.70 crore and owner PAT of ₹40.70 crore demonstrate scale-up; signed venue work supports a growth and special-situation thesis. The decisive risk is converting that expansion into owner cash: acquisition accounting, working-capital transitions and project funding are not sufficiently reconciled for a reliable group return estimate. At ₹510 on 19 October 2026, current-issued-share trailing P/E is 20.55x, but that is not a verified value signal. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS, with scored subfactors retained and G2 on Hold. A reconciled acquisition/cash bridge, project cash-cost schedules and entity-level claims would change the conclusion more than another headline order. An established compounder designation is not supported. [S1][S5][S12][S14]
score_note: Completed evidence-limited deep review. REV, CAP and valuation R/P remain NS; G2 is Hold. Canonical subfactors, coverage, bounds and linked diagnostic scenarios are retained; no numerical ranking.

gates.reason: No substantiated material diversion or repeated minority abuse identified. Disclosed contingencies, ordinary RPTs and a commercially explained auditor resignation are not themselves severe integrity failures.

Material receivable/advance stock-to-cash and acquisition/perimeter attribution remains unverified. The comparative CFO version change can be arithmetically bridged and is not itself a hold reason. Audits are unmodified and FY2026 total cash reconciles. G2 is an analytical evidence hold, not a fraud or missing-cash finding.

Known exercise cash and low starting debt support a funded conditional base, but committed-timetable bear and no-partner stresses have unfinanced gaps. Actual future facility access and project milestones are not verified; no demonstrated present default is asserted.

Observed trading on all 60 sessions supports a coarse reference-position test. BSE depth, surveillance, lot and lock-in status require implementation verification; status 6 in the NSE interoperation master means price discovery, not suspension.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Exhicon supplies event and exhibition infrastructure and is expanding into owned or operated venues, UAE contracting and aviation. FY2026 reported revenue of ₹202.70 crore and owner PAT of ₹40.70 crore demonstrate scale-up; signed venue work supports a growth and special-situation thesis. The decisive risk is converting that expansion into owner cash: acquisition accounting, working-capital transitions and project funding are not sufficiently reconciled for a reliable group return estimate. At ₹510 on 19 October 2026, current-issued-share trailing P/E is 20.55x, but that is not a verified value signal. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS, with scored subfactors retained and G2 on Hold. A reconciled acquisition/cash bridge, project cash-cost schedules and entity-level claims would change the conclusion more than another headline order. An established compounder designation is not supported. [S1][S5][S12][S14]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Exhicon Events Media Solutions Limited is identified by ISIN INE0O8901016 and BSE code 543895. It is treated as BSE SME: migration approvals do not prove completed migration. The information cutoff is 20 October 2026; the last market session is 19 October. The observed close of ₹510 and latest verified 16,397,100 issued shares imply ₹836.2521 crore market capitalization.

Financial scope is consolidated Indian GAAP/AS, with parent figures separately labeled. The analytical holding period is 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, the hurdle is 15% nominal annualized before investor taxes, and ₹5 lakh is an illustrative liquidity reference, not a user allocation. Confidence is High in identified signed statement values and allotments, Medium in cash-quality interpretation and secondary trading observations, and Low in acquisition-adjusted growth, project returns and a point valuation. Gates: G1 Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Conditional, G4 Conditional. No gate asserts current fraud, default or suspension. [S1][S8][S9][S10][S17][S18]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV NS, DUR 7, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 6 and EARN 6. IAS factors are R NS, D 3, P NS and L 8. BQS has a known contribution of 3.88 at 76% coverage, giving unrenormalized bounds of 4.12–6.28, not a point score. GQS has a known contribution of 2.60 at 45% coverage and raw bounds of 3.15–8.10; persistent CASH ≤3 caps its possible final upper bound at 5.00. Final GQS remains NS. IAS has 30% coverage, a known contribution of 1.40 and raw bounds of 2.10–8.40; Q, R and P are missing.

All three ranking flags are false. G2 and the relevant missing factors preclude ranking; NS does not mean a zero-quality company. Missing evidence receives neither a neutral 5 nor a renormalized average. No historical factor receives 9–10. Quality is not penalized for the quote, and scenario returns are not promoted into a supported R score. These score conventions are analytical heuristics, not validated return predictors. [S1][S2][S3]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
The parent designs, builds and services exhibitions, temporary and permanent venues, events and trade-fair media. Customers include organizers, trade associations, government/public mandates and corporate events. Collections depend on project milestones and post-event settlement rather than a pure prepaid subscription model.

The FY2026 group includes Maple Heights Business Centre (51%), Green Branch Contracting and Landscaping (76%), United Helicharters (80.51%) and Exhicon Global (100%). Venue development can yield upfront execution revenue and later O&M, but fee schedules are not sufficiently disclosed to call the entire portfolio annuity revenue. Aviation adds aircraft, maintenance, DGCA and tourism-seasonality risks distinct from event services. Broader Exhicon-branded hotels or group activities must not be included automatically: the FY2024 call expressly distinguished Thai hospitality interests. Foreign-currency units, elimination entries and ownership timing prevent a precise segment SOTP from the AOC-1 summary alone. [S1][S14][S15][S19]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is integration: reusable infrastructure, organizer relationships, design and execution staff, and venue access can reduce coordination costs and support repeat work. Named wins and delivered venues show access, not necessarily pricing power. Management’s historical claim of no competition is not adopted.

E-Factor supplies experiential and public events, Touchwood supplies event and wedding management, and Nesco’s established Bombay Exhibition Center demonstrates capable venue alternatives. These are contextual peers, not valuation clones: their asset ownership, customers, geography and minority structure differ. No peer multiple is transplanted. A 125,000 sqm development pipeline equivalent to 25% of a cited current national-capacity denominator is not 25% current operating market share. Independent repeat-customer cohort margins, tender-renewal economics and concentration are not quantified. MOAT 5 reflects a useful but contestable operating position. [S1][S14][S19][S20][S21][S22]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Reported consolidated revenue, in ₹ crore, was 9.4682 in FY2021, 46.3511 in FY2022, 58.8438 in FY2023, 88.4589 in FY2024, 143.5122 in FY2025 and 202.7005 in FY2026. Annual additions were 36.8829, 12.4927, 29.6151, 55.0533 and 59.1883 crore. FY2023–26 reported CAGR is 51.03%; FY2021–26 is 84.55%. The latter starts in pandemic disruption, while acquisitions and restructuring affect both windows.

Parent revenue rose from ₹37.2035 crore to ₹85.3018 crore over FY2023–26, a 31.86% CAGR, but absorbed businesses also change that perimeter. FY2026 H1 revenue of ₹102.6094 crore and H2 revenue of ₹100.0910 crore grew 63.83% and 23.75% against their respective comparable halves. These are half-years, not quarters. No FY2027 interim is used. Ten-year CAGR is ND, not reverse-engineered. A three-year window was chosen to avoid the pandemic base, but a reliable acquisition-adjusted demand cross-check remains unavailable. REV therefore stays NS rather than automatically receiving the ≥30% schedule’s starting score of 9. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Demand access is tangible but heterogeneous. ACMA selected 30,000 sqm of exhibition infrastructure for January 2027 delivery. The later AGM address describes a ₹50 crore asset retained by Exhicon and O&M across three editions, but does not disclose cash purchase cost or the fee economics. Mohali phase one has a ₹75 crore project estimate, a 65:35 Exhicon:IEML structure and a late-2027 target. Indore is described as developer-funded; it must not be modeled as another issuer-owned ₹75 crore project. Ayodhya land and Nashik arrangements are options until commissioning and contracts justify revenue.

UHPL’s 14 October Bell agreement has undisclosed consideration and regulatory completion conditions. The model links explicit budgets to collections, minority contributions and cash rather than extrapolating management TAM. GQS remains NS because REV and CAP cannot be established; persistent CASH 3 would cap a completed GQS at 5. The bottlenecks are committed capital, cash recovery and utilization, not simply announcing more square metres. [S12][S13][S14][S15][S24]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Governance is mixed, not a severe integrity finding. FY2026 statutory opinions were unmodified; the principal auditor relied on subsidiary audit reports furnished through management. The 30 June 2026 resignation cited increased work/resources and commercially inadequate remuneration, explicitly stated no other material reason, and marked information-denial questions not applicable. Bilimoria Mehta was appointed after the vacancy. Director/family remuneration in the group note totals ₹0.6288 crore. Ordinary related-party transactions and a disclosed intercompany UHPL advance do not establish diversion. March promoter shares were 7,283,498, or 49.32% of March capital; that is not a verified current percentage.

Dated delivery tests are mixed. June 2024’s approximately 50% annual growth aspiration broadly matches the 51.38% reported FY2024–26 CAGR, although acquisitions contribute. The below-60-day collection aspiration is not reflected in FY2026 ending group receivables of 157.21 days; the changed perimeter and ending-balance proxy limit like-for-like comparison. Pune and Greater Noida phase one are reported operating/completed. ACMA January 2027 and Mohali late 2027 remain future tests. The proceeds monitor reported no object deviation, not an independent audit of all cash. [S1][S6][S7][S11][S16][S19]

A public reproduction of two Delhi High Court orders dated 14 September 2026 records appointment of an arbitrator in the Inter Ads–Exhicon dispute. The orders expressly leave claims, counterclaims and merits open; they are not findings of misconduct or an adverse monetary award. The amount and subsequent arbitral outcome were not verified. [S26][S27]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY2026 operating EBIT is ₹49.4952 crore: ₹50.5002 crore PBT plus ₹1.7547 crore finance cost less ₹2.7597 crore other income. Operating EBITDA is ₹54.9076 crore. Group PAT of ₹45.2444 crore includes ₹4.5490 crore minority profit; owner PAT is ₹40.6954 crore. Effective tax was 10.41%. The diagnostic uses 25% operating tax rather than assuming the low rate persists indefinitely.

Reported CFO of ₹26.9408 crore includes ₹19.0823 crore bank borrowing within operating short-term liabilities. A two-sided transfer to financing leaves total cash unchanged and produces ₹7.8585 crore analytical CFO. Reported FCF, CFO less cash capex, is −₹19.9757 crore; the bank-reclassified proxy is −₹39.0580 crore before additional investment and advance claims. Latest-version FY2024–26 CFO/PAT is 0.276. Relocating the FY2025 bank repayment and FY2026 debt inflow gives 0.071. Original FY2025 CFO of ₹17.1278 crore and the later ₹26.5461 crore comparative are retained separately, not silently blended. The original cash-delta difference of ₹1.9639 crore equals its closing current-tax provision; the later comparative total cash reconciles. This is not a missing-cash allegation.

Receivables rose from ₹34.5666 crore to ₹87.3070 crore, an increase of ₹52.7404 crore, but the cash-flow movement is ₹20.0981 crore; the ₹32.6423 crore difference requires acquisition, FX or reclassification attribution. Almost all disclosed receivables are under six months, not all overdue. Average receivable days are 109.73, distinct from the 157.21 ending-balance proxy. Other current assets of ₹48.7796 crore include ₹14.8410 crore FDs, ₹23.9463 crore other assets and ₹1.2940 crore tax credits; ₹24.0496 crore short-term advances are not cash.

Defined operating capital, PPE including goodwill plus ONWC, rises ₹70.7913 crore to ₹188.6751 crore. Normalized NOPAT rises ₹24.6324 crore to ₹37.1214 crore: a 10.59% incremental accounting proxy versus 28.61% average-book ROIC. Neither is a mature-cohort project IRR. Every opening bucket is mapped once. Current tax of ₹5.5692 crore is separately paid, the ₹1.2940 crore credit is separately recovered, and ₹0.0160 crore deferred tax remains a terminal claim. Ordinary payables/provisions remain in opening and closing WC. Of ₹28.5690 crore cash/equivalents, ₹0.2492 crore FD is excluded pending availability; identified ₹1.78 crore monitored FDs are used only for eligible purposes at stated maturities. Other uncertain FDs and advances get no automatic liquidity or terminal recovery. Disclosed contingent claims total ₹4.6289 crore, separating parent/UHPL obligations and stated appeal status. [S1][S2][S3][S5][S16]

The FY2025 CFO version change is arithmetically bridgeable: start with ₹17.1278 crore, add ₹9.7393 crore for PBT versus owner PAT, add ₹0.1798 crore depreciation difference, subtract ₹0.7374 crore bank repayment, add ₹3.7530 crore reclassified short-advance outflow, subtract ₹5.4802 crore provision movement change and add ₹1.9639 crore tax-paid difference. The result is ₹26.5462 crore versus ₹26.5461 crore reported, a rounding difference. The remaining G2 issue is acquisition/perimeter attribution, not an inability to add these comparative cash-flow lines. [S1][S2]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
No supported point fair value or R score is issued. Two completed conditional methods are supplied: a linked operating/cash/terminal-multiple model and current-issued-share earnings/book cross-checks. Trailing P/E of 20.55x and March-book P/B of 4.19x use owner claims consistently. An EV multiple using group EBITDA without market-valuing NCI is not presented as comparable. The annual model starts on 31 March 2026, includes verified July/August exercise cash of ₹38.522925 crore, and ends on 19 October 2031 after a partial FY2032. FY2027 includes an undisclosed pre-entry period and is conditional, not an observed current-cash balance.

Base core growth is 20%, 18%, 15%, 12%, 10% and 8%; EBITDA margin moves from 24.5% to 23.5%; receivables move from 120 to 110 days; tax is 25%; ordinary capex is 5% of revenue. The ACMA ₹50 crore cash budget and helicopter ₹8 crore budget are analyst assumptions, not disclosed transaction costs. Mohali spends ₹25/50 crore with conditional 35% partner calls. Current bank debt is fully repaid in FY2027, with half-year interest; no unreceived promoter raise is used. At 14x terminal EBIT and an explicit approximate core NCI claim, the conditional base ends at ₹790.04 per share, a 9.15% annualized return. A funded delayed-project bear ends at ₹289.56, or −10.70% annualized; the 18x bull ends at ₹1,735.91, or 27.76%. These are diagnostic scenario outputs, not calibrated expected returns or trade targets.

At 14x, constant growth of about 19.12% reaches the 15% hurdle only if the other collection, cost and funding assumptions hold. The 12%/15%/18% hurdles imply conditional base entry prices around ₹448/393/345. Growth of 10–30% is crossed with 10x/14x/18x multiples. Additional tests cover cash access, legal settlement, NCI of 10–25%, ESOP dilution, ACMA budgets of ₹35/50/65 crore and helicopter costs. Proposed warrants pair ₹23.95 crore cash with 500,000 shares only in a separate conditional case. Missing entity-level cash/profit attribution and contractual costs prevent these calculations from becoming an IAS or actionable entry range. [S1][S7][S8][S9][S10][S12][S14][S15][S17][S23]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument is that profit growth may require repeated equity or debt funding while collection delays and owned venues consume cash faster than revenue converts. Under the original project timetable, the linked bear has a maximum ₹17.97 crore unfinanced gap and receives no shareholder IRR. A delayed-project and cancelled-helicopter alternative remains funded, but produces a 43.22% terminal-price loss in the conditional model and misses the original commissioning target.

Severe lower demand/margins, a 20% opening-receivable impairment, 25% cash-access haircut, cost overruns and absent IEML funding create approximately ₹120.16 crore combined gap; again, no IRR. Impairment reduces collectible opening stock, is added back once as noncash, and replacement WC is funded once. These correlated stresses are not evidence of an actual default. Even the base fails if receivables remain at 150 days or the ACMA cash budget rises to ₹65 crore with other assumptions unchanged. Minority shareholders bear residual dilution and earning-power loss after lenders and statutory/project claims. Collections, phasing and demonstrated venue cash profits are recovery routes. Impairment risk is High under these modeled dependencies. [S1][S12][S14][S15]

The later procedural arbitration orders add an unquantified claim uncertainty, not a proven liability. Separate ₹5 crore and ₹10 crore cash-charge tests are analyst sensitivities, not estimates of the claim or an award. No point valuation assumes this unresolved matter has zero economic effect. [S26][S27]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold shareholder wealth over five years require approximately 37.97% and 58.49% annualized returns before friction. At unchanged 16,397,100 shares, prices of ₹2,550 and ₹5,100 imply equity values of ₹4,181.26 crore and ₹8,362.52 crore. At 20x owner P/E, those outcomes require annual owner profit of ₹209.06 crore and ₹418.13 crore versus FY2026 ₹40.70 crore, roughly 39% and 59% profit CAGRs. Dilution increases the requirements.

The conditional bull does not reach 5×. Multiple expansion alone is not an operating thesis. A credible multibagger case would require much larger cash-generating venue capacity, demonstrated acquisition returns and financing that does not transfer the upside to new capital. No 5× or 10× designation is supported. [S1][S8][S9][S10][S17]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
These are research checkpoints, not an automated monitor or trading instruction.
1. Cash reconciliation: explain the ₹19.0823 crore bank-flow classification and ₹32.6423 crore receivable stock/flow transition. Unexplained recurrence keeps G2 on Hold.
2. Collections: FY2026 ending days are 157.21 and average days 109.73. The base assumes 120 then 110 ending days; remaining at 150 breaks modeled funding.
3. Other assets: document realizability and entity ownership of ₹23.9463 crore other current assets, ₹24.0496 crore short advances and FD restrictions. Do not credit cash automatically.
4. ACMA: verify January 2027 delivery, capital cost, three-edition O&M fees and payment milestones. A ₹65 crore cash budget fails the fixed-assumption base.
5. Mohali: verify the ₹75 crore budget, 65:35 calls and late-2027 target. Partner commitments are not money received.
6. Bell 206L4: verify consideration, maintenance investment, funding and DGCA completion. An agreement is not commissioning.
7. Capital: reconcile current promoter holdings, 15,400 residual old warrants, proposed 500,000 warrants and ESOP grants; distinguish issued and weighted shares.
8. Audit/claims: obtain an explicit acquisition/goodwill bridge and any orders on the ₹4.6289 crore disclosed contingencies. The existing audit opinion is unmodified.
9. Implementation: verify BSE lot, restrictions, lock-ins and live depth. Historical capacity is not a guaranteed exit. [S1][S8][S9][S10][S12][S14][S15][S17][S18]
10. Arbitration: verify claim/counterclaim amounts and any subsequent award or settlement. The September orders appoint an arbitrator without deciding the merits. [S26][S27]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved evidence, not a new-purchase recommendation. The framework matrix and compounder designation cannot be applied to incomplete BQS, GQS and IAS. Reported expansion and named projects deserve attention, but neither a reported P/E nor prospective main-board migration resolves cash and claim attribution. This is not Avoid — governance: no supported severe integrity finding exists. It is also not a demonstrated current funding failure; modeled shortfalls are conditional stresses with project-phasing and financing choices.

Keep the company outside numerical rankings until the material comparability and valuation gaps are resolved. A price decline alone cannot repair G2 or missing REV/CAP evidence. An existing holder needs actual-position liquidity and claim-specific facts before an implementation decision. [S1][S2][S5][S12][S17]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary annual reports, IPO-restated accounts, signed public filing mirrors, post-year allotments, JV documents and the 14 October helicopter announcement underpin the review. Secondary OHLCV supports the dated price and liquidity test. Undated intake figures are not treated as current evidence. Source entries distinguish full and partial inspection; decisive scanned cash-flow and contingency tables were checked visually.

The remaining questions are specific: the acquisition/noncash cash-flow bridge; organic revenue; entity-level cash, debt and NCI allocation; ACMA cash cost/O&M fees; helicopter consideration; bank maturity and usable facilities; current promoter/pledge/lock-in positions; and subsequent outcomes of disclosed contingencies. Original and later comparative accounts, issuer results, subsequent announcements and management explanations were checked. They provide context but do not supply the missing numerical reconciliations. Scenario budgets, margins, taxes, collection days, minority allocation, multiples and timing are analyst assumptions, not company forecasts or newly discovered accounting corrections. Moving bank flows between operating and financing categories changes no total cash. [S1]–[S25]

GOV.reason: Disclosed related-party remuneration, unmodified audits and proposed promoter funding support adequate conduct; broad acquisition accounting and repeated statement/capital-table inconsistencies limit confidence in disciplined stewardship. The outgoing auditor gave a commercial reason, not an information-access dispute; no severe integrity failure established.

MOAT.reason: Integrated infrastructure, event-organizer relationships and venue operating rights create useful execution advantages. Public and private alternatives exist, while independent pricing power, contracted retention economics and durable market share are unverified. Adequate differentiation, not monopoly.

REV.reason: Reported three-year growth is strong and both FY2026 halves grew. However, provisional acquisitions, disposals/restructuring and absorption into the parent prevent a reliable underlying comparable growth series. Pandemic five-year CAGR and parent-only CAGR do not cure this. NS rather than a neutral score or automatic9.

DUR.reason: Signed ACMA work, Mohali JV and developer-funded Indore route evidence multiple accessible demand channels beyond a TAM claim. Project timing, venue utilization and capital calls constrain duration; aviation is an additional execution risk. Strong accessible runway, not exceptional proven annuity economics.

CAP.reason: Book incremental NOPAT/IC proxy is about10.6% in FY2026 versus assumed14–18%capital-cost range, but acquired/reclassified capital and immature venues make it non-causal. Full acquisition allocation and project/unit returns are not disclosed, so the missing evidence cannot be replaced with5 or a high reported ROCE.

CASH.reason: Three-year conversion remains weak under original or latest comparative cash statements and after relocating bank flows to financing. FY2025 recovery and primarily recent receivables are contrary positives; FY2026receivables/advances and capex absorb funding. Persistent weakness supports GQS cap5, without alleging cash is missing.

BAL.reason: Low reported debt/EBITDA and verified post-year exercise cash provide a cushion; the claims-complete conditional base repays current bank debt without new financing. Collection/capex or partner-funding stress exhausts that cushion. Actual facility terms and fungibility remain unresolved, so resilience is mixed, not proven strong.

EXEC.reason: Reported growth broadly met the two-year growth aspiration and Pune/GreaterNoida phase-one delivery provides physical evidence. Cash-cycle aspiration was not reflected in ending group balances, while Mohali/ACMA and helicopter commissioning remain forward milestones. Mixed but meaningful execution.

EARN.reason: Operating EBIT, owner PAT and weighted diluted EPS grew; other income is not the main reported profit driver. Acquisition mix,10.4%effective tax and dilution make headline growth an incomplete normalized owner-earnings measure. No score9–10 based on short/changed-perimeter history.

R.reason: Conditional base diagnostic is not a defensible point group return because material cost, attribution and opening-to-current-cash inputs remain unverified. Do not map its illustrative9.15%return to a scored R.

D.reason: A funded but delayed-project bear has about43%terminal-price loss in the conditional model; the original timetable bear requires about18croreadditional funding and severe stress much more. These are analytical stresses, not a predicted default; verified capital raises and discretionary phasing are counterweights.

P.reason: The conditional reverse hurdle can be calculated, but unknown contracted economics and minority/cash attribution make a point expectations assessment insufficiently supported. A reported20.55xPE is not itself proof of cheapness.

L.reason: 60observed sessions give1.24theoreticalexitdaysat5%participation for the illustrative5lakhposition, startingband9. One-point downgrade for250sharelot granularity, recent locked-in allotments and absent executable depth/spread; no suspension inferred from status6.

BQS.reason: No renormalization; material missing factors remain NS. G2 hold excludes rankings.

GQS.reason: No renormalization; material missing factors remain NS. G2 hold excludes rankings. Persistent CASH<=3 caps possible GQS at5.
